speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the presence of leukocyturia, renal function impairment, and specifically the eosinophilic, binucleated cells found in your urine, I suspect this is drug-induced acute interstitial nephritis. Did you take any new medications, such as antibiotics or NSAIDs, shortly before these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to antibiotic hypersensitivity (amoxicillin/cephalexin). The presence of eosinophilic urine sediment ("eosinophils") following a rash and fever after antibiotic exposure is diagnostic. We will stop any remaining antibiotics and initiate supportive care; a repeat renal ultrasound will be requested in 48 hours to monitor hydronephrosis.
